<thought>Based on the strong M+1 peak (~16 % of the base) indicating many ^13C atoms, carbon is clearly present. The M+2 peak (~4–5 % of the base) matches the natural abundance of ^34S (≈4 %), indicating sulfur. No other element shows a characteristic isotopic pattern of sufficient intensity to be identified definitively. Therefore the elements that can be definitively identified are carbon and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
